chunks: From him, from al-‘Abbās, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Abū Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū ‘Abd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: A pond in which water collects—beasts urinate in it, dogs lap from it, and the person in janabah performs ghusl in it.
He said: “If it is the measure of a kurr, nothing makes it najis, and the kurr is six hundred ratls.”
Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: We have already explained the basis regarding this report earlier.

key_terms.رِطْلٍ: a unit of weight or measure used to define the amount of kurr
key_terms.كُرٍّ: a legal measure of water quantity that carries rulings of non-defilement
key_terms.مُجْتَمِعٌ: collected or accumulated in one place
key_terms.يُنَجِّسْهُ: renders it najis or ritually impure
key_terms.ٱلْجُنُبُ: a person in a state requiring ghusl due to janabah
key_terms.ٱلْغَدِيرُ: a pond or pool in which water gathers

ai.seo_question: When does collected water remain pure despite contact with impurities in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on water purity, stating that if collected water reaches the measure of a kurr, it is not rendered najis by such contact. It is significant in fiqh discussions of taharah, especially concerning the legal threshold for large quantities of water.
